name: Disorder with Optic Nerve Compression

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Criteria for Optic Nerve Compression

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of optic nerve compression on MRI or CT imaging
Presence of characteristic visual field defects consistent with optic nerve dysfunction
Optic disc pallor or atrophy observed on ophthalmological examination
Progressive decrease in visual acuity over time
Lack of inflammatory markers or signs of optic neuritis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological evidence of optic nerve compression plus at least one major clinical criterion (visual field defects or optic disc pallor)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of inflammatory or demyelinating optic neuropathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral optic nerve compression
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by imaging and clinical examination
searchTerms: optic nerve pressure on one or both sides
unilateral or bilateral optic nerve compression
eye nerve squeezing causing vision loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic visual field defects (e.g., central scotoma, arcuate defects)
searchTerms: specific vision field loss like central blind spots
visual field defects such as scotomas
loss of parts of vision field
pale or damaged optic nerve head
optic disc pallor or atrophy
optic nerve degeneration seen in eye exam
gradual worsening of eyesight
progressive vision loss
decreasing visual sharpness over time
difficulty distinguishing colors
color vision problems
color blindness or dyschromatopsia
unequal pupil response to light
pupil defect indicating optic nerve damage

occasional.symptomName: Diplopia due to extraocular muscle involvement
searchTerms: double vision from eye muscle problems
diplopia due to extraocular muscle involvement
seeing two images because of eye muscle issues
bleeding in the optic nerve
optic nerve hemorrhage
blood vessel rupture in eye nerve

rare.symptomName: Secondary optic neuropathy due to ischemia
searchTerms: vision loss from poor blood flow
optic nerve damage due to ischemia
reduced eyesight from optic nerve injury

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies other than optic nerve
searchTerms: paralysis of cranial nerves
weakness in facial or eye muscles
nerve palsy affecting face or head

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) to exclude optic neuritis
imaging: MRI showing compression of the optic nerve by mass lesions, vascular anomalies, or bony structures
CT scan demonstrating optic canal narrowing or fractures
other: Visual field testing confirming characteristic defects
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal nerve fiber layer thinning

distinguishingFeatures: Usually younger patients with acute onset

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe headache with visual symptoms
New onset of diplopia or cranial nerve palsies
